guide.axes.desc: Ranking everything by a single score narrows the view. Each perspective gets its own axis.
guide.axes.title: The 8 ranking axes
guide.axis.binge.desc: Works you cannot put down once you start
guide.axis.binge.label: Binge immersion
guide.axis.completed.desc: Finished works that are great to binge
guide.axis.completed.formula: Completion bonus + Bayesian rating×12 + completion rate×0.3 (completed works only)
guide.axis.completed.label: Completed binge
guide.axis.favorites.desc: The works readers bookmark the most
guide.axis.favorites.label: Bookmark surge
guide.axis.hidden.desc: Underrated works with few views but high ratings
guide.axis.hidden.label: Hidden gems
guide.axis.popular.desc: Combined firepower of views, bookmarks, and likes
guide.axis.popular.formula: (popularity percentile (exponential decay) × reach weight × trust factor × multi-platform + Bayesian adjustment) × serialization freshness
guide.axis.popular.label: Real-time popular
guide.axis.rating.formula: Bayesian rating (C·m derived from the catalog distribution) ×20 + log(rating count)×2
guide.axis.rating.label: Top rated
guide.axis.rookie.label: Promising rookies
guide.axis.trending.desc: Works with an exploding recent inflow
guide.axis.trending.formula: (rank rise×4 + trend×0.4 + popularity percentile×0.5×reach×multi-platform + Bayesian adjustment) × trust factor × serialization freshness
guide.axis.trending.label: Trending
guide.diagram.bayes.aria: Bayesian rating adjustment diagram: the fewer the ratings, the stronger the pull toward the prior mean
guide.diagram.pct.aria: Popularity percentile diagram: exponential decay makes only the top stand out
guide.diagram.pct.note: Little score difference at the bottom
guide.diagram.reach.aria: Reach weighting diagram: a #1 on Naver Webtoon weighs 1.00, a #1 on Lezhin Comics weighs 0.62
guide.diagram.reach.note: Even for the same “#1 on a platform”, the overall score differs by the scale of reach.
guide.diagram.trust.aria: Trust factor diagram: measured data is multiplied by 1.00 to 1.06 depending on rating count, estimated metrics by 0.78 to 0.80
guide.example.body: Every platform's #1 sits near a popularity percentile of 100. By percentile alone they would all tie, so a small-platform work with large estimated metrics could accidentally take the overall #1. Applying reach weight and trust factor as multipliers changes the story. The numbers below compare only the core component of the popularity score (popComp): both works are serialized on a single platform (multi-platform bonus 1.00), and the trust factors are example values within range. The actual popularity score adds a rating adjustment and multiplies by freshness.
guide.example.caption: Bar lengths are proportional to the popularity component (popComp), based on 105
guide.example.note: Even for the same “#1 on a platform”, the popularity component differs by more than twofold. Small platforms are not ignored — they rise legitimately on other axes such as genre and hidden gems.
guide.example.title: Example: why the overall #1 is not a tiny-platform work
guide.honesty.measured: star ratings are collected real data
guide.honesty.mid1: . Since Naver made its view and interest counts private, some supporting metrics such as views and interest counts are shown as
guide.honesty.mid2: . The same applies to some ratings, views, and completion rates on other platforms. Estimates are always clearly marked with the
guide.honesty.mid4: above also reduces their influence on rankings. We never inflate prices or view counts.
guide.honesty.title: We never mix measured data with estimates
guide.how.heading: The four mechanisms behind the rankings
guide.how.note: Every axis is a combination of these four. See “View formula” in each step for the exact calculation.
guide.lede: No ToonStudio ranking is picked by hand. Rankings are calculated only from a published formula, and that formula is written out on this page — because you should be able to verify for yourself why a work sits where it does.
guide.pillar.bayes.body: Which should you trust: a 5.0 from 3 ratings, or a 4.6 from 10,000? The fewer the ratings, the more the score is pulled toward the overall average; as ratings accumulate, it approaches the work's true score.
guide.pillar.bayes.formula: bayes = (C×m + average rating×rating count) / (m + rating count) — C·m is derived from the catalog distribution
guide.pillar.bayes.title: Bayesian rating
guide.pillar.percentile.body: View counts use different units on every platform, so direct comparison is unfair. We first rank popularity within each platform, then make only the very top stand out.
guide.pillar.percentile.formula: popComp = 100 × exp((percentile−100)/2.5) × reach weight × trust factor × multi-platform bonus (1.00–1.06) — popularity score = (popComp + rating adjustment) × freshness
guide.pillar.percentile.title: Popularity percentile
guide.pillar.reach.body: Even for the same “#1 on a platform”, the actual reach (traffic scale) differs. Multiplying by platform scale makes the gap between major and small platforms clear.
guide.pillar.reach.formula: reach weight = the maximum among the platforms the work is serialized on
guide.pillar.reach.title: Reach weight
guide.pillar.trust.body: Values we actually collected count with confidence; values filled in by estimation count slightly less. This is the safeguard that keeps estimated metrics from pushing measured works out of #1.
guide.pillar.trust.title: Trust factor
guide.reach.desc: We use the largest value among the platforms a work is serialized on. It multiplies into the popularity and trending scores.
guide.reach.title: Platform reach weights
